newsitem.title: USA: U.S. legislation introduced to revamp IRS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. legislation introduced to revamp IRS.

text.p: Members of Congress introduced legislation Wednesday to revamp the Internal Revenue Service just as lawmakers were preparing to vote on a package of new tax cuts.
The measure was based on last month's recommendations by a national commission calling for an independent board to oversee the agency and simplification of the tax code.

The bill would create a nine-member IRS oversight board appointed by the president and subject to Senate confirmation. Seven of the members would be from the private sector with expertise in managing large service organisations, a summary of the bill said. The two remaining board members would be the Treasury secretary and a member of the employees' union.
The IRS commissioner would be appointed to a five-year term and evaluated by the board, which would also have the authority to remove the commissioner.

The bill includes a goal of having 80 percent of tax returns filed electronically in 10 years. Incentives would include giving taxpayers an extra month, until May 15, to file electronic returns. The filing deadline for paper tax returns would remain April 15.
The legislation would require the IRS to develop procedures for accepting digital signatures for electronic filing.
The Treasury Department said it opposed the creation of an IRS oversight board when the national commission first proposed it.
The bipartisan bill requires a "Tax Complexity Analysis" for any legislative proposal that amends the Internal Revenue Code.
